_: Who is worth replying to on X, and who is not. Mate's call, 2026-08-22: 'I do not want to go behind other gurus when they are promoting their stuff, that is not nice. I really would like to focus on only folks and genuine questions. Less is more. The show is free, so promoting the show idea is fine.' That reverses how the follow list was going to be used — the big accounts are followed for the topical signal and because their replies are where the audience is, but the POST we reply to must be a real person asking a real question, never a guru's promo thread.
_watch: The accounts whose posts get read. PEOPLE, never brands — a brand account posts marketing by definition, so a reply under one is a reply under an advert. The second half of this list was found by SEARCHING for people talking about running a small business, not off a listicle: the listicle route produced 19 dead or wrong handles out of ~85, and a batch of startup founders who are exactly the tech crowd we are not for. Grew to 72 on 2026-08-22 from two more discovery sweeps (937 authors read, 33 kept): the yield is about 5% and falling, because X's population of non-technical people running small things is genuinely thin. Everything political, combative, adult, fan-account or tech-adjacent was dropped by hand — a follow is a public statement about what this account is, and X reads it as a topic signal.

queries.name: quoted-too-much
queries.q: ("quoted me" OR "charging me" OR "want to charge" OR "charge me" OR "asking for") ("for a website" OR "for a simple website" OR "for a landing page" OR "for an app" OR "for a booking system") -is:retweet lang:en
queries._: Somebody just quoted a lot of money for something small. The single most on-target moment there is.

queries.name: drowning-in-admin
queries.q: ("by hand" OR manually OR "copy paste" OR "copy and paste") (invoices OR bookkeeping OR "my spreadsheet" OR "client list" OR "every week" OR "every month") (hours OR tedious OR "sick of" OR hate OR "takes me") -is:retweet lang:en
queries._: Somebody doing by hand every week the thing a small tool would do once. Three clauses on purpose — two of them matched half of X.

queries.name: wish-a-tool-existed
queries.q: ("i wish there was an app" OR "i wish there was a tool" OR "why is there no tool" OR "why isnt there an app" OR "why is there no app") -is:retweet lang:en
queries._: A wish, unprompted. Only the long phrasings: bare 'someone should build' returned ten jokes out of ten.

queries.name: priced-out-of-software
queries.q: ("a month for" OR "per month for" OR "subscription for") ("a form" OR "a booking" OR "an invoice" OR "a simple" OR "scheduling") (ridiculous OR insane OR "cant afford" OR "too expensive" OR "so much") -is:retweet lang:en
queries._: Paying a subscription for something small. Same person as the quote one, a month later.

avoid._: A cheap first pass before the model, not the filter itself. Everything here is a phrase that is never worth a model call. The real filtering is triage, below — mate's rule about not turning up under people promoting their stuff is enforced there, where it can actually be judged.

pick._: Less is more, in his words. A handful of real replies beats a stream of them, and X demotes an account that looks like it is working the reply button.
pick._maxAuthorFollowers: Above about fifty thousand you are almost always looking at somebody with something to sell, and underneath them the reply is one of four hundred. The people worth answering are small accounts.
pick._oneReplyPerAuthorDays: Turning up under the same person repeatedly is the thing that reads as a bot, whatever the words say.
pick._maxRepliesOnPost: A post already carrying sixty replies is a thread, not a question. Nobody reads reply sixty-one.

draft._: How a reply is written. The show is free, so saying it exists is fine — but it is an offer, never a pitch, and it goes in at most one reply in three. The rest are just an answer.
rules: Answer the actual question. One specific, useful thing — not a summary of what they said.

NEVER invent his history. Do not write 'I built', 'I ended up', 'when I was', 'my client' or any specific personal anecdote — the model does not know what he has done and a made-up story under his name is the one mistake that cannot be walked back. Caught live on the first real draft, which claimed he had hosted and sold his own digital assets. Say what is TRUE OF THE THING instead: what is possible, what it takes, what usually goes wrong.
Never speak for anyone else's experience either. No 'most people find', no 'everyone I know'.
Plain spoken English, first person, the way you would text a friend. Lower case is fine.
Never compliment the poster. No 'great question', no 'love this', no 'so true'.
Never position yourself as an expert or a teacher. You are someone who has built the thing.
Never the words free, guaranteed or safe, and never claim anyone became a developer.
NO LINK, ever. X deprioritises a post carrying one, and a reply is the worst place to spend that.
If the show comes up at all, it is one clause at the end and it is an offer: they bring the problem, we build it on their machine, they keep it.
If you have nothing specific to say, say nothing — return an empty draft and it is dropped.

triage._: A keyword blocklist cannot tell a real question from noise — tested live on 2026-08-22 and the broad queries returned foot-fetish booking, a Jim Rohn quote and three crypto threads, all of which sailed through the block list. The model reads each candidate and answers one question. Anything not a clear yes is dropped, because dropping a good one costs nothing and replying to a bad one costs the account.
triage.question: Would a SMALL CUSTOM TOOL, built in an afternoon, solve this person's problem?
rules: genuine = a real person, describing their OWN recurring problem, that building something small would actually fix. They are doing something by hand, paying too much for something simple, or wishing a tool existed.

settings = a question about how to use an existing app — turning off read receipts, finding a menu, contacting support. Real people, but nothing to build. This is the trap: the first version of this filter passed five of these and zero of anything else.

promo = they are selling, promoting, or building an audience. A course, a waitlist, a newsletter, a 'DM me', a thread that exists to be bookmarked, or a success story being used as marketing. Mate's rule: we do not turn up underneath somebody who is selling.
noise = a joke, a quote, sport, crypto, politics, celebrity, or a fragment with no problem in it.
notforus = a real problem, but not one software fixes — medical, legal, relationship, a broken appliance.
When it is borderline, it is NOT genuine. Dropping a good one costs nothing; replying to a bad one costs the account.

genuine: i spend every sunday copying invoices from my email into a spreadsheet
got quoted 4k for a booking form. is that normal?
i wish there was an app that just told me which clients havent paid
settings: how do i turn off read receipts
is there a way to contact siteground
promo: a student with no coding experience launched a $10k app. here is how

_measured:
MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED — 2026-08-22, 168 tweets read across three live runs (~84c):
  open keyword search, broad queries .... 40 tweets → 5 kept, all 5 wrong (X-jargon collisions: 'receipts' means read receipts, 'quotes' means quote tweets)
  open keyword search, tight queries .... 28 tweets → 2 kept, both off-audience (a fasting app, a mass-unfollow tool). 15 of 28 were marketers using the exact language of the problem we want.
  reply sections of six followed accounts 100 replies → 0 kept. 96 noise, 4 promo. The reply section of a large business account is people saying 'so true' and other marketers.
TOTAL ON TARGET: 0 of 168.
The triage is not the problem — it correctly binned 163 of them and caught the 'settings' trap that the first version fell into. The SUPPLY is the problem: the people this show is for are not on X asking answerable questions in any volume. Do not build the approval page against this until a run produces candidates worth approving; it would be an empty page with a running cost.
